full_judgment:
The appellants contested the suit denying the material allegations and contending, inter alia, that the suit was barred by limitation and that the suit was not maintainable as there had been no proper acceptance of the bills of exchange. 

 The learned Subordinate Judge dismissed the suit on the finding that the bills of exchange were bills at sight which required acceptance by the drawee and as there was no such acceptance the suit failed for non-compliance with the provisions of Section 7 of the Negotiable Instrument Act. On the question of limitation, the learned Subordinate Judge found that the enhance claim made by the Respondent Bank by amendment of the plaint on the ground of devaluation of Pakistani currency was not sustainable as it was beyond the period of limitation but the limitation as to the original claim was saved by virtue of the operation of Section 14 of the Limitation Act. 

 “We do not see any reason why the trial of the plaintiff’s original claim by the learned Subordinate Judge should be barred by limitation. After the aforesaid amendment of the plaint, the suit being for a higher amount had to be taken cognizance of by the learned Subordinate Judge. But only after elaborately discussing the evidence, he concluded that the plaintiff was not entitled to the enhanced valuation. In our opinion, the trial of the original claim is in continuation of the suit originally filed by the plaintiff in the court of the local Munsif. Needless to say, the suit originally filed in that Court was within time.”
